text.content:
Storyteller guidance for running the non-Cainite supernatural creatures that share the Dark Medieval night, adapted from the crossover-lite rules in Faith and Fire. Use these as antagonist templates rather than as fully statted characters; scale Traits to whatever threat level the story needs.

Detecting the Supernatural with Soulsight

  • Demons/possessed mortals: A dark or smoky aura; the viewer needs a Mental Challenge or Occult x2 to recognize it as infernal.
  • Lupines: An unusually bright halo in either wolf or human form.
  • Ghosts: A weak, pale aura, even fainter than a vampire's (see also the detection rules under Ghosts, below).
  • The faithful (using their gifts): A bright golden halo.
  • The fae: Brilliant, swirling colors — and they resent being seen through their illusions.
  • Wizards (actively working magic): A sparkling halo.

Demons and Spirits

Demons rarely work directly; as "children of the Father of Lies" they tempt, mislead, and bargain rather than compel. Cainites hold little interest for them as victims (already damned), but plenty as servitors — the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} bloodline has served infernal masters since the Second City. Spirits and demons share four Traits: Willpower (spirit combat and general action, like a Physical Attribute), Rage (used to wound), Gnosis (Social/Mental challenges and Charms), and Essence (a pool combining the other three, spent to fuel Charms). Ratings typically run 1–10, with only the mightiest infernal dukes exceeding that.

Charms

  • Corruption: Works like the Dominate power Lure of Subtle Whispers, powered by Gnosis.
  • Disciplines: Demons may mimic Cainite Disciplines — commonly Animalism, Dementation, Mortis, Obfuscate, Obtenebration, and Presence — fueled by Essence, using Gnosis for the challenge.
  • Immunity to Fire.
  • Materialize: A rare, memorable event. Rage and Willpower set Physical Attributes; Gnosis sets Social/Mental Attributes. Most have vampire-equivalent health levels (more for powerful demons), and some regenerate a level of bashing/lethal damage per turn. Destroying a materialized demon's body only banishes it back to Hell to recover.
  • Possession: A Static Gnosis Challenge against the victim's Willpower; success grants control until the demon chooses to leave or is exorcised. Possessed hosts usually gain fire immunity and may channel other Charms.

Demons are vulnerable to True Faith and holy powers (which affect them at double effect) and are vain, arrogant creatures — flattery or exploiting their egos can undo careful plans. Demonic "investments" (granted powers) typically mimic Discipline effects up to Basic level (Advanced for the most powerful demons), grant Thaumaturgy/Mortis paths, or simply buy off Flaws or add Attribute Traits (usually up to two, three for powerful demons); nothing is free, and failing to honor the bargain causes granted power to fail or vanish at the worst moment.

Lupines (Werewolves)

Lupines rule the wild places outside Cainite cities and generally avoid dealing with vampires, though "Silver Fangs"/"Shadow Lords" nobles will occasionally negotiate. Their fighting orders (Fenrir in the Empire and points north, Fianna in Britain, or generically "Alroun") are ferocious even by frenzy standards.

  • Lupines shift between human, wolf, and a nine-foot battle-hybrid form. In hybrid form: Physical Traits double, fangs/claws deal aggravated damage, and the werewolf is treated as having Might. Mortal witnesses effectively suffer Rötschreck and forget the encounter once it ends. Only beast-related or other-Lupine Social/Mental Attributes and Abilities function in this form. True wolf shape uses the same benefits as the Protean power Form of the Beast.
  • Many Lupines can detect Cainites with low Road ratings or infernal ties and attack on sight; @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} and those on the Road of the Beast are only rarely attacked.
  • Lupines heal normal damage at one level per turn. Fire, silver weapons, and the teeth/claws of other supernatural creatures (including vampires) deal aggravated damage they cannot heal this way.
  • Rage (2–4 minimum Traits, regained when injured or humiliated) fuels extra actions exactly like Celerity (one Rage Trait per action) and can heal one health level instantly once Incapacitated (not aggravated damage).
  • Gnosis (3–5 minimum Traits per session, regained through rest, meditation, and communing with spirits) fuels powers resembling Animalism, Auspex, Celerity, Obfuscate, Protean, and occasionally Thaumaturgy.
  • Lupines frenzy as readily as the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} and suffer no wound penalties while frenzied. They can enter the spirit world, becoming invisible and intangible (like Auspex's Anima Walk) without leaving their bodies behind.

Wizards and Sorcerers

Three broad types populate the setting: wise women/folk magicians (herbalism, charm-craft, fortune-telling, often condemned by the Church despite their harmless intent), mages (scholarly practitioners, often gathered in secret orders such as the Order of Hermes, which considers the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} abominations and wages a hidden shadow war against them), and infernalists (those who genuinely traded their souls for power). Mechanically, adapt Thaumaturgy or Mortis paths, requiring time, props (herbs, candles, a lock of hair, ritual texts), and a spent Willpower Trait per casting (fewer props and less time needed as the caster grows more skilled).

Ghosts

Ghosts share the same Willpower/Rage/Gnosis/Essence Traits as other spirits but are otherwise mostly harmless to the living, tied to the mortal world through emotional anchors (people, places, objects). Destroying all of a ghost's anchors condemns it to eternal torment; resolving them grants a chance at redemption and peace. Ghosts are strongest at places of death (battlefields, graveyards, murder sites) where the veil is thin.

  • Detecting a ghost with Soulsight requires a successful Mental Challenge; the ghost gains a three-Trait bonus for breaking ties. Even then, understanding what's being seen requires Occult x3 or one level of Lore: Ghosts.
  • Ghost powers commonly resemble Auspex, Chimerstry, Dominate, Obtenebration, Presence, and the Thaumaturgy path Rego Motus, fueled by Essence.
  • Barring specific wards, a ghost can travel anywhere it wishes in the mortal world.

Faeries

The Dark Ages fae are not the Banality-touched changelings of the modern game — the Shattering has not happened, and they need no mortal disguise. Two courts hold seasonal sway: the mischievous but less cruel Seelie (spring/summer) and the monstrous Unseelie (autumn/winter, home to trolls, ogres, goblins, imps, and redcaps).

  • Most fae have Chimerstry-like illusion powers, plus a mix of Animalism, Auspex, Celerity, Dementation, Dominate (especially Reveler's Memory), Obfuscate, Obtenebration, Presence, and Protean; ogres and trolls may have Fortitude and Potence, and noble fae often wield Thaumaturgy-like paths (especially Creo Ignem and Rego Tempestas). All are fueled by Glamour (typically 3–5 Traits per session).
  • Fae heal bashing/lethal damage like mortals (often faster, via their own healing magic) but suffer aggravated damage from fire and cold iron; merely touching cold iron costs a true fae a Willpower Trait per round of contact.
  • Attacking a noble fae in her own court requires first winning a Social Challenge against her.

Cross-Type Interactions

When a power calls for a target to spend a Trait type she doesn't have (e.g., a Discipline requiring Blood Traits used on a Lupine), substitute Gnosis/Glamour/Essence/other Traits as applicable, or Willpower if nothing else fits; conversely, a Kindred asked to spend a foreign Trait type may substitute Blood Traits (this does not apply to powers that simply drain a Trait as damage). If a vampire power tries to induce frenzy or Rötschreck in a creature that can't normally experience them, treat the effect as @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.derangements.JournalEntry.24f1647439f64eb6]{Crimson Rage} or another appropriate derangement for the power's duration instead.

Drinking Other Supernaturals' Blood

Vitae from another supernatural type does not purge normally — "first in, last out": a Cainite cannot rid herself of a Trait of foreign blood until all vitae she held prior to drinking it is spent first.

  • The Infernal: Ordinary infernalists' blood is unremarkable; materialized demons cannot be drained at all (they are pure spirit), and attempting it is likely to end badly for the vampire.
  • Werewolves: Each Trait of Lupine blood counts double, but the drinker must test for frenzy immediately and carries the Negative Trait Impatient until the blood is spent. Particularly potent blood (Pure Breed x3+) may grant bonus Potence or Celerity levels at Storyteller discretion.
  • Mages/Sorcerers: Causes strange visions or hallucinations; effects are entirely Storyteller discretion.
  • Fae: Counts double like Lupine blood and grants a temporary derangement (Storyteller's choice) plus further strange side effects until the blood cycles out.
  • Numinous mortals (True Faith): Actively harmful — each Trait drunk inflicts one Trait of aggravated damage on the drinker.

Embracing Other Supernaturals

The Embrace was never meant for beings with no connection to humanity, so attempts on other supernatural creatures almost never succeed.

  • Lupines: A Static Gnosis Challenge; win means a quick, painless death, tie means a slow and painful one. On a loss, if the Storyteller allows it, an Abomination results — it loses Garou regeneration and society benefits but keeps any known Gifts and can use vitae like a Cainite. Both Cainites and werewolves hunt Abominations on sight.
  • Other shapeshifters: Often simply produce a corpse; some ignite in flame, killing the shapechanger and inflicting five levels of aggravated damage on the would-be Embracer.
  • Mages/sorcerers: Produces a mortal-knowledge-only vampire with no functional magic; any Numina the mortal had do not survive the Embrace.
  • The Infernal: Impossible — demons have no blood as such.
  • True fae: The fae simply dissolves into formless glowing mist.
  • A vampire's own ghoul: Produces an ordinary vampire who keeps her learned Disciplines (counted against the three learned at character creation) — the one sane, sensible outcome on this list.

vtmlarp.source: Faith and Fire (Dark Ages Vampire), Chapter Seven: Allies and Antagonists
